introH2: 🗺️ Why does choosing the right area in Uttaradit matter so much?
introHtml: In Uttaradit, where you stay really does shape the trip, because the main draws sit in different zones. Uttaradit city centre (the Borom-At Road–Clock Tower district) is the hub for malls, Khlong Pho market, food and both the train and bus stations — ideal if you want to explore the city, pay respects at the Phraya Phichai Dap Hak monument, or use Uttaradit as an onward base. Laplae old town, about 8 km from the city, is a district of old wooden shophouses, the town gateway and the Tin Chok woven-cloth museum — best for travellers into heritage streets and photography. And the Sirikit Dam zone in Tha Pla district, about a 45-minute drive away, sits close to the dam crest, reservoir boat trips and nature — best if you're here to relax by the water. Many people book in the city expecting an easy drive to Laplae or the dam, then burn hours driving back and forth. This guide rounds up 12 Uttaradit hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Uttaradit has no metro; you get around by car, and the province is spread out enough that your choice of area sets up the whole trip. City-centre stays are the most convenient, with Friday department store, Khlong Pho market and restaurants within walking distance, and the train and bus stations close by — great if you don't have a car. Stays in Laplae old town (Si Phanom Mat) let you walk to the town gateway and museums within the district, but it's about 8 km from the city. Almost everything in the Sirikit Dam zone (Tha Pla district) needs a private or rental car, as it's a separate district about a 45-minute to 1-hour drive from the city. The areas in this guide: City Centre — malls, markets, food, the train station · Laplae Old Town — old wooden houses, the town gateway · Sirikit Dam — a waterside base for boat trips and nature.

entries.addr: 204 Thesaban Si Phanom Mat Rd, Si Phanom Mat, Laplae District, Uttaradit
entries.storyHtml: Laplae Guesthouse is the top score in this guide — Agoda 9.4 · Booking 9.0 — a guesthouse inside a roughly 80-year-old wooden shophouse in the heart of Laplae old town, just a walk from the Laplae town gateway and the Tin Chok woven-cloth museum. This isn't a standard hotel; it's a wooden house that keeps its vintage character throughout, with mosquito-net beds, fans and retro decor. Real guest reviews praise the 'just like grandparents' house' atmosphere, the very warm owners, and the bikes you can borrow to explore the old town. But understand that it's an old wooden house — simple rooms, none of the usual hotel amenities, and it's in Laplae district about 8 km from the city. Best for heritage-street travellers and photographers who value atmosphere over luxury.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Borrow a bike and ride the old town in the early morning or evening when it's cooler — the wooden houses and town gateway photograph beautifully. It's an old wooden house with few rooms, so book ahead, especially during festivals and long weekends. Without a car you'll need to connect from the city into Laplae, so allow time.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Uttaradit hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in within Uttaradit?
faq.a: It depends on your trip. The city centre (Borom-At Road–Clock Tower) suits city sightseeing, malls and food and works without a car, with the Friday store, Khlong Pho market and the train station (Seeharaj, Friday, Ton Thong, Sunee). Laplae old town suits heritage-street travellers and photographers (Laplae Guesthouse). The Sirikit Dam zone (Tha Pla district) suits travellers here to relax by the water and visit the dam (Baan Na Pasiri, Sirikit Dam Guesthouse).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Uttaradit hotels cost?
faq.a: Mostly affordable: budget stays and guesthouses start around ฿400–600/night (Thaimit ฿400, Friday ฿450, Areena ฿490, Laplae Guesthouse ฿500). Mid-range hotels and resorts run about ฿595–850 (Ton Thong, ARAYA, Barista, Sunee, Seeharaj). The riverside resort near the dam tops out around ฿1,200 (Baan Na Pasiri). All are approximate starting rates for standard rooms — compare all 3 sites before booking.

faq.q: ❓ Visiting Laplae old town — where should I stay?
faq.a: Laplae old town is in Laplae district, about 8 km from the city. If old-town sightseeing and photography are your main goal, stay in that area for the full atmosphere — Laplae Guesthouse ฿500, a guesthouse in a roughly 80-year-old wooden shophouse, a walk from the town gateway and the Tin Chok woven-cloth museum, with bikes to borrow. If you also want to stay in the city, pick a central hotel with parking and drive over to Laplae for the day.

faq.q: ❓ Using Uttaradit as a base for Sirikit Dam — where should I stay?
faq.a: Sirikit Dam is in Tha Pla district, about 45 minutes to 1 hour from the city. If visiting the dam and relaxing by the water is your main goal, stay in that zone to cut the drive — Baan Na Pasiri Resort ฿1,200, a Nan River resort ~13 km from the dam with a water park and activities for families, or Sirikit Dam Guesthouse (EGAT) ฿700, where you actually sleep inside the dam grounds with reservoir views. Both need a private car.

faq.q: ❓ Is Uttaradit easy to get around without a car?
faq.a: Uttaradit has no metro, so without a car staying in the city centre is the most convenient — Seeharaj and Friday walk to the mall, Sunee walks to Khlong Pho market, all close to the train and bus stations. Stays in Laplae old town, the Sirikit Dam zone and the suburbs (Areena, Barista, ARAYA) have few nearby shops, so come with a car or have Grab ready.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Uttaradit hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary by promotion at any given time, so we recommend comparing all 3 before every booking — each review page in this guide includes price-comparison links, which can save you hundreds of baht per night, especially during the Laplae durian season and long weekends when rooms fill fast.
